title: Molecular autonomous agents.
abstract: I consider an autonomous agent to be a physical system able to act on its own behalf, such as a bacterium swimming up a glucose gradient. I tentatively define an autonomous agent to be a system capable of self-reproduction and at least capable of performing one thermodynamic work cycle. I give a hypothetical chemical example. I then explore the increasingly odd implications of this definition.
journal: Philosophical transactions. Series A, Mathematical, physical, and engineering sciences
